title: SQL injection via f-string interpolation of user_id
body: get_user() builds the query with an f-string: cur.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}"). user_id is passed directly into the SQL text with no parameterization, so any caller that passes attacker-controlled input reaches the database unsanitized. An attacker supplying a user_id like "1 OR 1=1" or a UNION-based payload can read arbitrary rows from the users table (and potentially other tables via UNION SELECT), or use stacked/boolean techniques to exfiltrate data. Fix: use a parameterized query, e.g. cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,)).
